== Formal definition ==

Let $(F,+_F,\cdot_F,>_F)$ be an [[field (mathematical concept)#Ordered_field|ordered field]]. Let $\ge_F$ denote $>_F \lor =$.

$a_1\in A$ is the '''maximum''' of set $A \subseteq F$ if

$$
\forall a \in A, a_1 \ge_F a
$$

the '''minimum''' of set $A \subseteq F$ if

$$
\forall a \in A, a \ge_F a_1
$$

<blockquote>
If $A$ is finite, then logically there should always be '''one or more''' maxima and minima. However, this is not always the case when $A$ is an infinite set.

{{Hidden example}}
Consider the set

$$
\{x \in \mathbb{Q} | x^2 < 2\}
$$
{{End hidden}}

When a maximum or minimum exists, it is always simultaneously the [[supremum and infimum|supremum or infimum]] of the set.
</blockquote>

<ref>{{#cite:Q2396}}</ref>
